transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-22
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~44m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Head of ML - Lark), Priya Singh (Platform Eng - Lark), Alex Moreno (CTO - Lark)

Summary: quick integration discovery focused on how Lark would connect via SDKs and via LangChain/LlamaIndex, whether to use Hosted or Dedicated for latency/cost, and Private deployment constraints (VPC egress, KMS). SE to produce examples and vendor docs; AE to follow up on pricing and SLA.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joinin. i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the account owner. Lucas is our solutions engineer. how's everythin on your side?
[00:08] Jordan Patel: hey, thanks, Maya. i'm Jordan. we also have Priya and Alex on. all good. we wanted to run through integration options; we have a client-facing search/chat product and we're evaluating both Hosted and Dedicated.
[00:15] Alex Moreno: hi team. main concerns are latency spikes during peak retail hours, data residency for EU customers, and also minimizing engineering lift.
[00:22] Lucas Rivera: great, we'll try to cover those. quick question on workloads — are you mostly generation/chat, or embeddings + semantic search?
[00:30] Jordan Patel: primary is embeddings for product search, then a chat assistant for post-purchase support. embeddings at scale — batches of 10k docs per day, roughly 50M tokens/month.
[00:40] Priya Singh: and we do nightly reindexes, plus realtime single-document embeds triggered by user actions. we also have strict PII masking requirements.
[00:48] Lucas Rivera: ok, that helps. on SDK support: Redwood has official SDKs for Python, Node, and a REST API. we also have example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex — small sample repos that show the auth flow and streaming.
[00:58] Maya Chen: i'll share those repos after the call. Lucas, can you highlight the LangChain/LlamaIndex pattern quickly?
[01:06] Lucas Rivera: sure. (slight audio rustle) so most folks wrap Redwood's REST/SDK inside LangChain's LLM wrapper or LlamaIndex's indexers. we provide an LLM client that returns token-streaming compatible iterators, and an embeddings client that mirrors the embeddings API. for auth you can use API keys, or for Dedicated/Private we integrate with your internal token broker via a proxy.
[01:28] Jordan Patel: what's the recommended pattern for us? we prefer using LangChain in our ingestion pipeline and LlamaIndex at the app layer.
[01:35] Lucas Rivera: common approach: ingestion pipeline uses the embeddings client directly with our Python SDK — that's straightforward. For app layer, put a small auth gateway behind your app that proxies requests to Redwood using a service credential; that lets you rotate keys and enforce RBAC. For Hosted, we support signed short-lived tokens too.
[01:55] Priya Singh: about that gateway — our security team requires no direct egress from our VPC for production data. would a proxy in our VPC that calls Redwood Hosted be acceptable?
[02:05] Maya Chen: yes, that's a common pattern. if you want zero egress, Private (VPC or on-prem) is recommended; otherwise you can host a proxy in your VPC that calls Redwood Hosted with TLS. note you'll still have egress but it's via your managed proxy.
[02:18] Alex Moreno: what about Dedicated? is Dedicated in our own VPC or in Redwood's cloud?
[02:23] Lucas Rivera: Dedicated is tenant-isolated GPU pools we reserve for you; networking can be configured with private peering or customer-managed VPC depending on the contract. you can choose whether to keep inference endpoints inside your network via private peering (reduces egress exposure) or use Redwood-managed endpoints with encryption in transit.
[02:40] Jordan Patel: latency-wise — at peak we need p50 <= 120ms for short completion calls. is that realistic on Hosted?
[02:47] Lucas Rivera: depends on model and sequence length. for smaller open models and with our caching/batching, Hosted can hit that but p95 is tougher during noisy periods. Dedicated gives you capacity guarantees and more predictable latency; Private on-prem can be tuned further but is heavier ops.
[03:05] Priya Singh: can you do per-route quotas? we want to throttle support chat but allow search embeds higher throughput.
[03:12] Maya Chen: yes, we support per-route rate limits and token quotas per API key. you can also do token budgets per route in the console.
[03:20] Jordan Patel: observability — we need traces tied to our request IDs and per-token cost breakdowns for billing.
[03:26] Lucas Rivera: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, latency, per-model charts, and distributed tracing hooks. we emit request_id in response headers and you can forward that into your tracing system. for Private, we can ship a trace collector sidecar or integrate with your existing OpenTelemetry stack.
[03:41] Alex Moreno: any client example for OpenTelemetry?
[03:44] Lucas Rivera: yes, we have an example repo that shows injecting request_id and using OTEL spans around the call. i'll attach that.
[03:50] Priya Singh: about embeddings throughput — do you support async/batch endpoints? we want a bulk ingest path for nightly jobs.
[03:58] Lucas Rivera: embeddings have a batch API designed for high throughput. Dedicated gives you guaranteed concurrency and autoscale policies, Hosted has soft limits that can be raised via request. for very large nightly jobs, many customers run an internal worker that retries with backoff and hit Dedicated endpoints or use a parallelized uploader.
[04:16] Jordan Patel: rate limits impacts — if we hit a quota, how are failures surfaced? can we fallback to cheaper model variants?
[04:24] Lucas Rivera: failure modes: you'll get 429 or queued delays. Redwood also supports automatic fallback rules — route to a cheaper model if the primary is at capacity. that's configurable in the routing policy.
[04:34] Maya Chen: on security compliance — are you SOC2/ISO attested?
[04:38] Lucas Rivera: yes, Hosted and Dedicated are SOC 2 Type II compliant; we also have ISO 27001. Private deployments can operate in a customer's compliance boundary; we provide audit logs and KMS integrations. i'll send the SOC2 report stub after call.
[04:50] Priya Singh: for Private deployment, how does KMS integration work? we use AWS KMS + HSM for encryption key management.
[04:58] Lucas Rivera: we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments; keys never leave your account for on-prem. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via a secure key exchange depending on the model.
[05:08] Jordan Patel: ok great. a couple of product questions — does Redwood support streaming responses for chat? and function/tool calling?
[05:15] Lucas Rivera: yes streaming is supported in both SDKs and REST. function calling is supported as structured output; we also have a tool-calling pattern with typed JSON responses. the SDK returns chunked events for streaming so LangChain wrappers can consume them incrementally.
[05:28] Alex Moreno: about LangChain/LlamaIndex — any special quirks for vector store compatibility? we use FAISS in prod.
[05:34] Lucas Rivera: nothing special — embeddings are standard float vectors. we provide numpy/pytorch friendly outputs and examples for storing into FAISS and Chroma. LlamaIndex connectors are prebuilt for direct ingestion.
[05:44] Jordan Patel: curious about billing granularity — can we tag requests to attribution at customer or tenant level?
[05:50] Maya Chen: yes, you can set metadata tags on requests and in the console we have per-key and per-route cost breakdowns. we also support invoice-level attribution for Dedicated contracts.
[05:59] Priya Singh: network constraints again — we have a strict rule: no 3rd-party SaaS in our EU prod environment. That pushes us to Private. what would be the typical timeline to stand up a Private VPC deployment?
[06:10] Lucas Rivera: Private VPC typically takes 6-12 weeks depending on sizing and approvals — you'll need to provision peering, provide IP allowlists, test egress rules, and do a security review. we have a checklist we share. Dedicated can be spun up in 2-4 weeks for initial capacity. Hosted is immediate.
[06:23] Jordan Patel: can we run a proof-of-concept on Hosted first to validate latency and embeddings quality before committing?
[06:27] Maya Chen: absolutely. many customers start with Hosted POC, run a few benchmarks, then move to Dedicated or Private once they hit scale or compliance needs.
[06:34] Alex Moreno: any bench tools you provide? we want to run p50/p95 tests with our prompt set and synthetic load.
[06:40] Lucas Rivera: we have a benchmark harness and we can run a joint benchmark — we can also share a jupyter + load scripts. Lucas: i'll run an initial internal sim with your prompt set if you share it.
[06:50] Jordan Patel: on SDK auth — you mentioned short-lived tokens for Hosted. what's the rotation story?
[06:55] Lucas Rivera: Hosted supports short-lived tokens via our token service; you can mint per-session tokens with limited scope. For Dedicated/Private we recommend a proxy that mints service-level tokens or integrate with your OIDC provider.
[07:07] Priya Singh: crosstalk — (laughter) sorry, quick question on quantization — do you have recommended model + quant settings for CPU fallback?
[07:13] Lucas Rivera: for CPU or lower-cost inference we recommend 4-bit quantized variants for certain open models; Redwood Optimize will recommend profiles based on your workload, and we can provide quality vs cost tradeoff charts.
[07:25] Maya Chen: ok want to move to wrap up and next steps. Lucas, confirm what you'll deliver.
[07:29] Lucas Rivera: i'll send: 1) LangChain/LlamaIndex example repos with proxy patterns, 2) OpenTelemetry sample, 3) benchmark harness + sample load scripts, 4) Private deployment checklist. target by Friday next week.
[07:41] Maya Chen: i'll send Hosted vs Dedicated pricing bands and SOC2/ISO docs by Thursday. Jordan, Alex, Priya — anything else?
[07:48] Jordan Patel: please include sample env var patterns and the recommended retry/backoff recommended config for batch embeddings. also include guidance for per-route quota setup.
[07:58] Priya Singh: and a network diagram example for the proxy pattern and private peering.
[08:03] Alex Moreno: we'll share a small subset of our prompt set and a couple of sample queries within two business days.
[08:10] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the SE implementation workshop.

[08:20] -- (end of recorded portion, brief off-mic)

Notes about transcription: there are a few minor transcription errors — some product names were transcribed inconsistently (e.g. "KV cache" heard as "K-V chase"), timestamps approximate.

References shared: "LangChain connector repo (link)"; "Private deployment checklist (doc link)"; "SOC2 overview (doc link)"; "Benchmark harness (repo link)"

Recap (verbatim):
- POC path: start Hosted POC with benchmark harness + prompt set.
- If compliance requires, move to Private (6-12 weeks). Dedicated is middle ground for capacity and predictable latency (2-4 weeks to provision).
- Integration: use Redwood SDKs for embeddings + LangChain/LlamaIndex wrappers; proxy pattern recommended for auth and key rotation; per-route quotas and routing policies supported; observability via request_id and OTEL integration.

End transcript
